features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Look for proofreading accuracy and overall professional finish; this captures whether the letter reads as careful, credible, and easy to trust.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors are distracting enough to undermine professionalism or carefulness.
Several noticeable errors are present, but the letter remains understandable.
Only minor or isolated errors appear, with generally polished presentation.
The letter is essentially error-free and reads as highly polished.

features.evidence: 3 to 7 years launching 2 to 6 production services
features.name: Production service record
features.description: Look for years of professional software work plus repeated responsibility for testing, maintaining, and launching production systems; this captures the depth of real-world delivery experience behind the application.

levels.descriptor: Professional production experience is unclear, very limited, or not tied to shipped systems.
Shows baseline production experience but with relatively modest tenure or service scope.
Shows solid multi-year responsibility across several production services.
Shows extensive, repeated production ownership across many launched or maintained services over a longer span.

features.name: Advanced degree level
features.description: Look for the highest relevant academic qualification stated; this captures how far the applicant exceeds the role's minimum educational baseline.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is made clear.
Shows a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical preparation.
Shows a relevant master's degree.
Shows a relevant doctoral degree.

features.evidence: Go is my principal programming language
features.name: Go centrality
features.description: Look for how strongly the letter positions Go as a core production language rather than a peripheral skill; this captures fit to the role's explicit Go requirement.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or only implied.
Go is mentioned, but the letter does not show it as a main working language.
Go is clearly presented as a primary production language with meaningful use.
Go is framed as a core specialty or daily driver tied to sustained production ownership.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Look for concrete Python use in services, tooling, automation, or analysis; this captures how strong the applicant's Python capability appears for the role's back-end and agent work.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned.
Python is mentioned only briefly or without concrete usage.
Python is shown as a substantial language for tooling, services, or automation.
Python is presented as a deeply used production language with clear engineering rigor or broad internal impact.

features.evidence: automated the intake and triage of vulnerability reports
features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Look for direct experience automating vulnerability intake, classification, routing, or deduplication; this captures hands-on relevance to one of the team's central workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Mentions security automation in general, but not a clear triage workflow.
Gives a concrete example of automating vulnerability intake or triage.
Shows end-to-end triage automation with specific functions such as classification, routing, deduplication, or clear operational impact.

features.evidence: Python agents plan and act while Go services provide the guardrails
features.name: Agentic tooling ownership
features.description: Look for explicit design or implementation of agent-based systems, especially with Python agents and Go control layers; this captures direct fit to the job's agentic tooling mandate.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is described.
Mentions agents or agentic work vaguely, without clear ownership or architecture.
Describes a clear agentic system the applicant designed or built.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agent architecture with concrete attention to constraints, permissions, auditing, or supervision.

features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Look for evidence of shipping AI or LLM systems in production, especially with reliability measures; this captures whether AI experience goes beyond buzzwords to operational competence.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
AI or LLMs are mentioned only generically, with little operational detail.
Shows direct experience building or shipping AI-backed production features or workflows.
Shows production AI experience plus evaluation, hardening, reliability work, or explicit management of failure modes.

features.evidence: threat models and targeted reviews with remediation
features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Look for concrete security review work such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or fix validation; this captures how directly the applicant has done assessment work rather than only adjacent engineering.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is described.
Claims assessment experience, but with little detail about what was done.
Describes concrete assessment activities such as threat models, reviews, or validation of fixes.
Shows repeated, structured assessment practice across multiple systems with attacker-minded analysis or explicit remediation follow-through.

features.evidence: replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms
features.name: Algorithmic rigor
features.description: Look for specific examples where data structures or algorithm choices materially improved a system; this captures the depth of practical problem-solving beyond a generic claim of strong fundamentals.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of algorithmic or data-structure skill is provided.
Makes a general claim about strong fundamentals without a concrete example.
Provides one substantive example of algorithms or data structures improving a system.
Provides especially convincing or repeated examples showing algorithmic choices materially changed performance, correctness, or tractability.

features.evidence: too many signals, too few experts
features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Look for how clearly the letter articulates the underlying security-operations bottleneck this team addresses; this captures strategic understanding of why this work matters.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role in generic software or security terms without identifying a specific operational problem.
Mentions automation or scale as desirable, but without a clear bottleneck or systems view.
Identifies a concrete problem such as manual triage, repetitive analysis, or scarce expert capacity.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about scaling security judgment through workflows, tooling, or variant analysis across the development lifecycle.

features.evidence: make the secure path the easy path
features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Look for language about helping product engineers adopt secure defaults rather than being policed after the fact; this captures whether the applicant sees security as an enabling product for developers.

levels.descriptor: Shows little indication of a developer-facing security philosophy.
Expresses general interest in secure development, but not much about developer workflows.
Clearly frames the goal as making secure behavior easier, more routine, or more default for engineers.
Consistently emphasizes developer empathy, workflow fit, and security as enablement rather than compliance or after-the-fact policing.

features.evidence: improvements are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Look for explicit attraction to foundational infrastructure whose benefits spread broadly; this captures whether the applicant is motivated by central platform impact rather than only local feature work.

levels.descriptor: No clear interest in foundational or multiplier-effect work is shown.
Shows general excitement about scale or impact, but without a platform rationale.
Explicitly prefers foundational systems because improvements help many teams or users.
Builds a strong case that platform leverage is a core career motivation, not just a passing interest.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Look for recurring adversarial practice such as CTF participation or other attacker-minded exercises; this captures whether the applicant has actively trained the offensive perspective relevant to security engineering.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Mentions occasional CTFs or a general attacker mindset without much depth.
Shows regular CTF participation or other recurring offensive practice.
Shows strong offensive credibility through top placements or especially serious attacker-oriented practice.

features.name: Security certification level
features.description: Look for formal security credentials and their practical rigor; this captures whether the applicant adds third-party validation of security knowledge beyond self-description.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security credential is mentioned.
Shows a baseline credential such as Security+ or similar fundamentals-oriented certification.
Shows a hands-on practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.
Shows multiple relevant credentials or an advanced credential paired with especially strong practical security evidence.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Look for responsibility in public codebases, from patch submission to release management; this captures external engineering credibility and maintainership habits.

levels.descriptor: No open-source involvement is mentioned.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or one-off contributions.
Shows regular contributions or recurring stewardship in open-source work.
Shows maintainer-level ownership with reviews, releases, roadmap, or community responsibility.

features.evidence: distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics
features.name: Personal systems ambition
features.description: Look for the technical ambition of side projects, especially systems work with real failure modes or infrastructure complexity; this captures self-driven depth beyond the day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or straightforward personal app.
Mentions a substantial side project with meaningful engineering complexity.
Mentions an ambitious infrastructure or distributed-systems project tackling hard issues like failover, recovery, consistency, or semantics.

features.evidence: the queue went from a dreaded chore to something the tooling mostly runs itself
features.name: Achievement specificity
features.description: Look for whether claims are backed by concrete examples, mechanisms, or outcomes rather than generic adjectives; this captures how evidential and believable the letter feels.

levels.descriptor: Mostly presents aspirations or broad qualities without concrete evidence.
Lists relevant experiences, but with limited detail about what was done or achieved.
Provides at least one concrete example tied to a task, architecture, or outcome.
Repeatedly substantiates claims with specific before-and-after effects, implementation details, or operational results.
